text:
The take that many NVIDIA supply deals were "a handshake with Jensen, not a written contract" is half right.

Jensen did made the big calls in the room. CEOs of some of NVIDIA's largest customers told me that this past week. Billion-dollar commitments, made on the spot. I'd bet suppliers saw the same. That is hard to replace.

What's overstated is the risk to the biggest deals. They're on paper.

• NVIDIA disclosed $279B in supply and capacity commitments as of July, up from $119B a quarter earlier, driven by memory. $267B of it is scheduled through fiscal 2029. You can’t report it without more than a handshake. 
• NVIDIA became TSMC's largest customer in 2025. The two biggest HBM suppliers are tightening contracts so buyers can't back out. Suppliers aren't the flight risk.
• I've said supply and the roadmap are mostly set for at least 18 months.

The real exposure is the next round: anything not on paper, and whether NVIDIA keeps committing at Jensen's pace. Rivals will bid for whatever it doesn't.

NVIDIA has a deep bench, and Colette Kress has been on calls reassuring suppliers. Tuesday's $NVDA call, her first as interim CEO, is where she shows who makes the big calls now.

Ship 42 returned from orbit and was caught by the launch tower arms at Starbase around 4:20 p.m. ET, roughly 22.5 hours after liftoff.

SpaceX had planned to catch both stages, but the Super Heavy booster was diverted offshore after its catch was aborted.

THE HARDEST TAPE IN YEARS. 

This is not the worst market, but arguably the hardest one to win in. $NBIS can rally double digits one day and give it all back over the next two. $SPY and $QQQ reclaim key levels only to lose them again. Earnings beats are getting sold, misses are getting rewarded, and even strong guidance is no guarantee of a rally. Meanwhile, sticky inflation, rising yields, uncertainty around the Fed, and the leadership shock at $NVDA have added another layer of unpredictability. The AI story hasn’t disappeared, but the market has moved from asking who benefits from AI to who ultimately pays for it. Capex, debt, funding and cash flow now matter as much as demand. In this environment, being right about the company, the earnings, or even the macro isn’t enough if the market disagrees with your timing. You can get four out of five things right and still lose money. That’s why this is a market for discipline, patience and proper position sizing, not oversized conviction. Know what you own, know why you own it, keep cash available, and don’t let short-term volatility force long-term decisions. Easy markets make everyone look like a genius. Difficult markets reveal who actually has a process. The edge right now isn’t predicting every move. It’s surviving the uncertainty long enough for your thesis to play out.

en_summary: Explains Starship’s plasma blackout and why SpaceX lands it with engines instead of parachutes for Mars, quoting Kate Tice on reentry.
text:
Starship’s plasma blackout explained, and why SpaceX lands it with engines instead of parachutes for Mars:

Kate Tice: “Reentry is typically a portion of flight where we don’t have communications with the spacecraft, because it’s reentering at or around orbital velocity. That’s roughly eight kilometers per second, or about five miles per second. And at those speeds, the spacecraft is moving through the atmosphere so quickly that a plasma field around the vehicle starts to develop.”

Jessie Anderson: “And that blanket of plasma distorts communication frequencies, so it’s not uncommon to experience brief blackouts in communication.”

Jessie Anderson: “Starship is designed to land on Mars, where there are no runways or other humans to help out. So we’re doing propulsive landing instead of more traditional means like parachutes. That’s because propulsive landing enables more rapid reusability.”

NVIDIA: LITIGATION HISTORY AND THE SIDE C QUESTION (1/3)

Date: November 14, 2026

Grades used throughout: VERIFIED means a primary document (filing, court order, executed agreement, SEC release) states it. REPORTED means a credible secondary source states it and no primary document was located. NOT FOUND means the searches returned nothing. ESTIMATE means a figure constructed from market benchmarks, labeled as such.

BOTTOM LINE

• Nvidia historically carried entity securities coverage inside a conventional layered D&O tower: its early 2000s tower contained a policy written around securities claims, the entity slot in that era's standard ABC form.
• Nvidia has been sued in four federal securities class actions and has never settled one, so no insurer has ever funded a securities settlement for it, and the absence of such a payment proves nothing about coverage either way.
• Its one documented fight with its D&O carriers was offensive, not defensive: in 2005 Nvidia sued its own carriers when they resisted paying defense costs on the 3dfx creditor claims.
• Today the Financial Times reports a Side A only program, which, if accurate, is a change from Nvidia's own historical posture; the record does not date the change.

OPTICAL NETWORKING DAILY DIGEST, SATURDAY, NOVEMBER 14, 2026

STATUS CHANGE

• Cisco Systems: Cisco's first quarter fiscal 2027 earnings call on November 12, 2026 added vendor-stated optics detail to the results reported on November 12, 2026. In Q&A, Robbins stated: "The design win we had this quarter at the 1.6 Terabit optic was a client side win. And it was our first client side optics win at this particular hyperscaler." The hyperscaler was not named. CFO Mark Patterson stated on optics: "We actually had a $1 billion quarter, just last quarter on the optic side," referring to the fourth quarter of fiscal 2026, and said the first quarter of fiscal 2027 was a record first quarter for optics.
